content.comment_body: Hello, I have an older [product_name] operator device and a basic [product_name] module with screen, both purchased several years ago but unused until now. The operator device powers up and the screen and cursor keys work (but only as expected in certain screen areas). However, the ENTER key does nothing. I can ping the [product_name] module's IP using the operator device as a switch, and link LEDs appear fine. I'm wondering if the device is set to an operational mode by default, preventing the use of the ENTER key, or if there's another step needed to activate admin functions. If anyone has advice or knows how to change to admin mode (if that's even possible), I'd appreciate the help. Thanks!
The operator device does not have different modes like operator or admin; only the [product_name] module has those. Are both devices set up on the same IP subnet?

Hi [user_name], Could you clarify whether your operator device is truly brand new or possibly used before? The ENTER key on these devices is typically the most used and should function even when simply powered. Test gently pressing the key—you should feel resistance and a faint click, which can be compared to other keys. If there's no response and the key feels pressed in, the keypad membrane may be faulty, for which there's no official replacement. Technically skilled individuals might attempt repairs or external wiring, but that's only advisable for experienced electronics technicians. Regards, [user_name] (translated by Google)

I'm connecting the module and operator device directly via a single patch cord – there's no Ethernet switch. However, I can't access the IP configuration screen on the operator device. I tried pinging the operator device with my laptop using 192.168.0.1 (which I read is a default factory IP), but got no response.

To clarify, the device really is unused and was purchased from an authorized dealer; it's just been stored in its box for a while, but never operated until now, so I don't expect any storage damage. The ENTER button does make a click and feels correct when pressed, so it seems the control isn’t blocked mechanically. It feels more like it's not permitted to work due to firmware or some configuration parameter I can't check. Notably, after the backlight goes off, every button besides ENTER turns it on again when pressed. The behavior makes me question if the button itself is faulty, but I don’t understand why. Advice is appreciated.
You haven't yet answered my direct question: what is the IP address and subnet mask assigned to the [product_name] module?

Hello [user_name], Thanks for joining in, I know you're a knowledgeable [product_name] hardware user. While I'm not at the system now, the usual settings are: IP 192.168.0.3, mask 255.255.255.0, gateway 192.168.0.10. The module is in admin mode—I confirmed that by stopping the program and scrolling to where it prompts to switch to operator mode. As mentioned, there's no Ethernet switch or router; both units connect using a direct Ethernet cable. My goal is to use the operator device as a switch, with the spare port for service via laptop. I can't get into the LOGO SELECTION screen during initial power-up, whether the module is connected or not, and thus can't configure IP, subnet mask, or gateway settings for communication between the two. I can use the device as a network switch—I'm able to ping the module when it's connected through the operator device and my PC. Attempts to ping the operator device with presumed factory IP (192.168.0.1) haven't worked. Accessing the LOGO SELECTION screen seems to rely on the ENTER key, which I can't activate, but I'm unsure if that's the only way. That's why I sought help here. Sorry for not answering earlier and thank you for your expertise. If sharing the module's mask leads to a fix, I'd be genuinely impressed.
Any updates? I provided the information you requested earlier, and I appreciate your help.

Unfortunately, I can't offer a solution since I'm not familiar with this particular issue of a non-working ENTER key on a new operator device. According to your details, both devices are on the same subnet and should communicate successfully. You may want to contact [company_name] support for further assistance.

Thank you [user_name]. For reference, I still can't view the network settings on the operator device since I can't access LOGO SELECTION. That's the main challenge—entering those configuration menus. I'll try contacting [company_name] support.

Hi, rather than lengthy troubleshooting, please try the following: 1) Start the [product_name] configuration software, switch to network mode, and click 'Go Online'. You should be able to see both your module and operator device, and adjust IP settings using the settings tool. 2) On the module, switch to STOP mode and ensure you're in admin (standard password is LOGO or your own) not operator mode. Change it if needed. 3) Refer to the official manual for step-by-step instructions on configuring the operator device. PS: I've never heard of a newly unpacked operator device with a non-working keyboard. Hope this helps.

The operator device with article number [article_no] is too old to be scanned with [product_name] configuration software. For scanning ability, you need the updated model with article number [article_no].

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering a significant functionality problem with the [product_name] operator device: the ENTER key does not respond, preventing access to critical configuration screens like network or module selection, and blocking IP setup. While basic inputs, display, and network switching work, without the ENTER key, the device cannot perform its intended control or configuration role. The cause is unclear—whether hardware (keypad or membrane issue), firmware lockout, or misconfiguration—and there isn't a straightforward way to diagnose it. The device can't be configured as needed and is effectively unusable for its main purpose.
analysis.user_expectations: Users assume a brand new [product_name] operator device is ready for use immediately, with all input keys—including ENTER—working upon power up, allowing access to all setup and network menus without initial troubleshooting.
